16.0.s.en: (1) The portion of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in general

16.0.0.en: The Jordan by Jericho: the part of the Jordan River adjoining Jericho.

16.0.1.en: The water of Jericho: the spring adjoining Jericho whose waters the prophet Elisha healed (2 Kgs 2:19-25). Toward the sunrising: that is, the eastern border of the land of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, which lies in the east of the land of Canaan. The wilderness: the desert adjoining Jericho.

16.0.2.en: He mentions the borders of the lands of the two sons of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh who lived west of the Jordan, because the first half of the tribe of Manasseh lived east of the Jordan (Num 32). For Joseph took two portions, that is, double that of his brothers, as Jacob had promised him because of his piety and righteousness (Gen 48:5, 6). The border begins from the Jordan River adjoining Jericho and extends to the spring of Jericho, then to the desert adjoining it, which lies in the east of the land of Canaan (Map 8).

16.1.0.en: Ataroth: a town lying south of Bethel and about 11 km north of Jerusalem, on the border between Ephraim and Benjamin.

16.1.1.en: The border extended from Bethel, which was built beside Luz and where God appeared to Jacob in the ladder, and the border extended to the city of Ataroth, in which the Archites lived, from whom came Hushai the Archite, the counselor and friend of David the prophet, who defeated the counsel of Ahithophel (2 Sam 15:32).

16.2.0.en: The border extended westward to the Japhletites, who are among the Canaanite tribes, that is, the original inhabitants of the land. Then it extended to the city of Beth-horon, which lies on low ground, because there is a city of the same name lying on high ground, which lies 19 km north of Jerusalem. Then the border extended to Gezer beside Horon, lying about 29 km northwest of Jerusalem.

16.2.1.en: So we find that the goings out of the border of the tribe of Ephraim, that is, its beginning, are at the Dead Sea, and then it extends northward beside the Jordan River.

16.3.0.en: This is the portion of the tribe of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh, and it lies north of the portion of the tribe of Judah, and their lands were fertile.

16.3.1.en: God's blessings are many for His pious children. Just as He gave a double portion to His son Joseph, He still singles out His pious ones with spiritual and material blessings. Fear God and trust that you will enjoy greater care from Him, and He will provide all your needs.

16.4.s.en: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

16.4.0.en: After mentioning the portion of the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh in general, he mentions here the borders of the portion of the tribe of Ephraim, which extended east from the city of Ataroth-addar, mentioned in (v. 2), to the upper Beth-horon, that is, the one lying on high ground (v. 3) (Map 8).

16.5.0.en: The border extended westward toward the Mediterranean Sea to the town of Michmethah, then turned back and went east to Taanath-shiloh, that is, the entrance of Shiloh. Shiloh became the seat of the tabernacle of meeting until the days of Samuel the prophet, then afterwards it was moved to Nob, then Gibeon, and finally David moved it to Jerusalem. Then the border extended to the east of a town called Janohah.

16.6.0.en: Then the border went down from Janohah to Ataroth. This Ataroth lies close to the Jordan River and is different from the one mentioned in (vv. 2, 5). Then it went to Naarath, which is close to Jericho in the valley of the Jordan. Then it reached the city of Jericho, lying five miles west of the Jordan, then extended to the Jordan River.

16.7.0.en: The border extended to the city of Tappuah, which lies at a distance of 13 km from Nabulus, then turned west to the valley of Kanah, and the valley of Kanah is known today by the same name; the border of this valley of Kanah reaches the Mediterranean Sea at the city of Joppa. As for the border of the portion of Ephraim, it reached only the valley of Kanah and did not extend with it to the sea.

16.8.0.en: The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh living west of the Jordan was large, so some of its cities were given to Ephraim his brother by Joshua's appointment and allotment, as is made clear in (ch. 17). It is to be noted that Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, so he took his portion in the midst of this tribe, but he did not take it until after the distribution of the portions of all the tribes, as is made clear in (ch. 19:49, 50). This shows the servant's putting his brothers before himself.

16.9.0.en: The tribe of Ephraim was lax in driving the Canaanites out of its lands, and they remained living in Gezer, and the tribe used them as slaves. The rest of the tribes fell into this same error, and these pagans became a snare to the children of Israel, for they mixed with them and intermarried with them and worshiped their idols, so God abandoned them, as will appear in the Book of Judges.

16.9.1.en: I wish you would put others before yourself, whether in material distribution or in honor and praise, so that you win everyone and acquire humility and receive many blessings from God.

16.9.2.en: The portion of the western half tribe of Manasseh

17.0.s.en: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

17.0.0.en: Here he speaks in general terms about the portion of the tribe of Manasseh, who was the firstborn of Joseph and took a portion like the rest of Joseph's brothers, although the tribe of Ephraim his younger brother took a larger portion according to the prophecy of Jacob his grandfather (Gen 48:19). Manasseh had one son, Machir, who was distinguished as a brave man of war (Num 32:33-42), so half the tribe of Manasseh, that is, half the sons of Machir, possessed a portion east of the Jordan in the days of Moses, in the land of Gilead and Bashan. The land of Gilead is so called either after a person named Gilead who lived there anciently before the sons of Jacob, or after Gilead the son of Machir who lived in these lands east of the Jordan (Map 7).

17.1.0.en: Here he mentions the son of Machir, who is Gilead, and his six male sons.

17.2.0.en: Here he makes clear that the sixth son of Gilead is Hepher, and this Hepher begot Zelophehad and no other. And Zelophehad begot five daughters, that is, he had no male descendants.

17.3.0.en: The five daughters, who were of the descendants of Zelophehad, came forward and asked Joshua and Eleazar the priest to fulfill the promise of Moses to them to give them a portion in the land of Canaan like the rest of their cousins (Num 27, 36:10-12).

17.4.0.en: In this way the tribe of Manasseh received ten portions that it possessed west of the Jordan, five of them for his five sons and the other five for the daughters of Zelophehad, so the total portion of Manasseh west of the Jordan is ten portions, that is, shares.

17.5.0.en: In this way the daughters of Zelophehad possessed lands within the tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, on condition that they marry their cousins so that their portion would not pass out of the tribe of Manasseh. This is in addition to the portion of Manasseh east of the Jordan.

17.5.1.en: Demand your right and God will help you, especially when you demand your spiritual rights, to receive a portion and membership in the Church, so that you enjoy God's care and peace.

17.6.s.en: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

17.6.0.en: Asher: a city about 25 km east of Shechem (Nabulus).

17.6.1.en: Michmethah: a city lying beside Shechem to the east.

17.6.2.en: This land corresponds to the part lying east of the Jordan, and it is bounded on the north by the portion of the tribes of Issachar and Asher, on the south by the portion of Ephraim, and on the west by the Mediterranean Sea. Shechem, which is present-day Nabulus, is counted among the most important cities; in it are the bones of Joseph, and in it were the tents of Abraham and Jacob, and in it Joshua read the Law to the people. Shechem became the capital of Israel (the northern kingdom) in the days of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and it was defiled by him and by his idols, whose worship he introduced into Israel.

17.6.3.en: The border extends from the east to a town called Asher, then Michmethah, and after that to Shechem, then turns to the right, that is, to the south, to reach the town of Tappuah (ch. 16:8).

17.7.0.en: The tribe of Manasseh possessed the lands surrounding the city of Tappuah. As for the city of Tappuah itself, it belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.

17.8.0.en: The border extended southward, heading to the south of the valley of Kanah, and this valley of Kanah is a vast plain extending to the Mediterranean Sea. There was a watercourse passing between the cities of Manasseh. It is to be noted that in this region the cities of Manasseh are mixed with the cities of Ephraim (Map 8).

17.9.0.en: Here he confirms the position of the portion of Manasseh among the tribes: the portion of Ephraim was south of the valley of Kanah, while the portion of the tribe of Manasseh was north of this valley, that is, the portion of Ephraim lies south of the portion of Manasseh, and in the west of the portion of Manasseh lies the Mediterranean Sea, while on its north was the tribe of Asher on the western side and the tribe of Issachar in the northeast.

17.10.0.en: The tribe of Manasseh was numerous, so Joshua gave it some cities lying on the border between it and the tribes of Issachar and Asher lying to its north. These cities are:

17.10.1.en: Beth-shean: it is now Beisan, which is 6 km from the Jordan River, together with its villages and fields. Ibleam: beside the city of Jenin.

17.10.2.en: Dor: a city lying on the Mediterranean Sea (ch. 11:2, 12:23). Endor: it lies 9 km southeast of Nazareth. In it was the witch to whom Saul went, and there the prophet Samuel appeared to him (1 Sam 28:7). Taanach: it lay within the borders of Issachar.

17.10.3.en: Megiddo: it was a great city with an ancient civilization.

17.10.4.en: The three heights: what is meant is the last three cities, which were built on high ground, and in them the worship of the pagan gods was offered on the high places.

17.11.0.en: The tribe of Manasseh was lax and afraid, so it did not drive out the Canaanite inhabitants from these lands, but lived with them.

17.12.0.en: After the tribe of Manasseh grew strong, it was content to take tribute from the pagan inhabitants of the land, and this is a great error, as we mentioned, into which the children of Israel fell. So they mixed and intermarried with them and worshiped their idols, and God was angry with them and humbled them and strengthened the original inhabitants of the land against them, as appears from the Book of Judges.

17.12.1.en: If God gives you strength and zeal for life with Him, do not be lax and lose this opportunity, but rise and drive out from yourself your old evil thoughts and bad habits, for God supports you and awaits your love and your rejection of evil for His sake.

17.13.s.en: (3) The demand for a larger portion

17.13.0.en: One lot: although Joshua had given them two portions, that is, a portion for Manasseh and a portion for Ephraim, yet joined together they express the smallness of this portion by saying one lot and one portion, that is, it is small, as if it were one portion.

17.13.1.en: The sons of Joseph joined together, the number of the sons of Manasseh being 52,700 persons and of the sons of Ephraim 34,500 according to the census of the Book of Numbers (ch. 26), and they came forward complaining to Joshua, asking for additional space in the land because of their large number.

17.14.0.en: Mount Ephraim: a mountainous region with fruit-bearing trees lying in the midst of the portion of the tribe of Ephraim. The mountain was so called because it lies in the portion of Ephraim and because it has fruit trees on it, since the word Ephraim means fruitful.

17.14.1.en: Joshua asked them to go to the forests in the high mountains of Ephraim and cut down the trees that bear no fruit in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, and destroy its original inhabitants living in the midst of the forests, who are the Perizzites and the Rephaim, so that it would become land fit for dwelling and they could dwell in it.

17.15.0.en: They objected that the Canaanites were strong, armed with chariots of iron, so they could not drive them out and possess their lands, nor could they live with them, for the mountain would not hold them both. This shows Ephraim's weak faith in the power of God, who is able to support them in driving out the enemies.

17.16.0.en: Joshua said that these two great tribes really needed additional land, which they would obtain by their own effort from the lands of the mountain, and he made clear to them that the mountain and its outgoings, that is, what lies beyond it, were theirs, and that the iron chariots cannot travel on the mountain and in the forests on it, but travel only in the level valley, so there is nothing to fear from them there.

17.16.1.en: By this Joshua stirs them up to rely on God and go forward, because they are a great people, and to drive out the Canaanite tribes living there.

17.16.2.en: We often make excuses of weakness, as Satan deceives us about the danger of striving. But we can do all things in Christ who strengthens us.

17.16.3.en: The portion of the tribe of Benjamin

18.0.0.en: The congregation of the children of Israel assembled, that is, the Jews belonging to the seven tribes that had not yet possessed land, and their assembly was in a city called Shiloh, which is a city in the middle of the Promised Land, and they set up the tabernacle of meeting there so that it would be easy for all the tribes to reach it. The tabernacle of meeting had previously been at Gilgal for about six years, which is beside Jericho and the Jordan River, and the tabernacle of meeting remained about 300 years at Shiloh until the Philistines seized the ark of the covenant in the days of Eli the priest and Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 4); then David brought the ark of the covenant back to Jerusalem and set up the tabernacle there (2 Sam 6). The assembly of the children of Israel before the tabernacle of meeting was so that the division would take place in the presence of the Lord. The Canaanite tribes had submitted to the children of Israel and surrendered, and some fled, but some regions were still possessed by these tribes. So the submission was partial and not complete, and the land would be divided on condition that each tribe complete the driving out of the remaining Canaanites.

18.1.0.en: The seven remaining tribes are: Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan, and they will take their portion as mentioned in (ch. 18, 19), because the other five tribes took their portion east and west of the Jordan as mentioned in the preceding chapters.

18.2.0.en: Joshua rebuked the rest of the tribes for their laziness in possessing their portion in the land of Canaan and in clearing the remaining parts of the Canaanite inhabitants, because God's promise is true: He had given it to them, that is, He is ready to help them in possessing the land and driving the wicked out of it.

18.2.1.en: Joshua's rebuke is a type of the rebuke of Christ Jesus to those invited who excused themselves from attending the wedding (Mt 22:3).

18.2.2.en: I wish you would begin every work with prayer so that God may intervene, and know that prayer does not make unnecessary the work that follows it, but blesses it.

18.3.s.en: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

18.3.0.en: Describe it according to their inheritances: divide the land into seven parts so that each part may take a portion of it by lot.

18.3.1.en: Joshua asked the heads of the seven tribes to choose three men distinguished by diligence and precision, so that a group of 21 men would be formed to survey the remaining land of Canaan and divide it into seven parts to be distributed by lot to the seven remaining tribes.

18.4.0.en: After the remaining land is divided into seven parts to be distributed among the tribes, the tribe of Judah would be in the south of the land of Canaan, and north of it would lie the house of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh that possessed land west of the Jordan, because the other half tribe of Manasseh possessed land east of the Jordan.

18.5.0.en: The method of division was carried out by surveying the land in all its regions and writing a description of its contents of cities, rivers, farms, pastures and valleys, then casting the lot so that God would determine for each tribe a region of the land.

18.6.0.en: As for the Levites, they have no portion in the land, but are given cities with their pastures to live among the tribes in the land of Canaan, as will come in (ch. 21). And we do not forget that two and a half tribes had received their portion east of the Jordan from the hand of Moses.

18.7.1.en: The delegates did that as Joshua said. It is clear that they had learned the principles of surveying and measurement from the Egyptians during their sojourn in Egypt, and they brought what they had written to Joshua so that he might cast the lot before the Lord and determine the place of each tribe.

18.7.2.en: God's grace and protection of this group appear, for the owners of the pagan land did not molest them.

18.7.3.en: In the division, not only the area was taken into account, but also the extent of the good things of the land, in water and crops, that is, in all respects.

18.7.4.en: And after the division by lot, Joshua took into account the number of each tribe, so he gave the large tribe in number a larger area, taking it from the tribes smaller in number.

18.7.5.en: Know that God chooses for you your position in life, so do not murmur or worry, for you are the right person in the right place according to God's plan for your salvation and the salvation of the world.

18.8.s.en: (3) The portion of the tribe of Benjamin

18.8.0.en: Beth-aven: it lies about 9.5 km east of Bethel (ch. 7:2). Luz: Bethel, lying midway between Jerusalem and Nabulus.

18.8.1.en: Ataroth-adar: it lies about 11 km north of Jerusalem (ch. 16:2). The nether Beth-horon: it lies about 12 km northwest of Jerusalem (ch. 10:10). Baal: also called Jearim, one of the cities in the portion of Judah and near Jerusalem (ch. 15:9). The well of the waters of Nephtoah: it lies northwest of Jerusalem (ch. 15:9). The valley of the son of Hinnom: it lies south and west of Jerusalem (ch. 15:8), and north of it live the Rephaim and south of it the Jebusites, who are among the original inhabitants of the land.

18.8.2.en: Geliloth: it is the same as Gilgal, their first center before Shiloh (ch. 4:19). The shoulder: a projection in the high land lying north of the Arabah, that is, the valley (ch. 15:6). The location of the tribe of Benjamin was fixed as a peacemaker between the two quarreling tribes, Ephraim in the north and Judah in the south, and God gave it a small land according to its number, but a distinguished one:

18.8.3.en: 1- Because Jerusalem, the city of the great King, lies in it.

18.8.4.en: 2- Because it is high land, so it is easy to defend it with a small number of inhabitants.

18.8.5.en: 3- It is surrounded by hills that make access to it difficult and under watch.

18.8.6.en: Therefore we notice the skill of the sons of Benjamin in fighting and in archery, as will appear in the battles of the Book of Judges (ch. 20). The borders of Benjamin were the Jordan River on the east, as far as its mouth into the Dead Sea, and on the west the portion of the tribe of Dan, on the north the portion of the tribe of Ephraim, and on the south the portion of the tribe of Judah. The cities mentioned here were mentioned in (ch. 15) because they are the same as the borders of the tribe of Judah (Map 8). It is to be noted that the tribe of Benjamin lies beside Shiloh, which lies in the tribe of Ephraim, where the tabernacle of meeting was, then in the days of David the tabernacle was moved to Jerusalem, which lies in the portion of the tribe of Benjamin. In this the prophecy of Moses in his blessing of the tribe of Benjamin is fulfilled, where he said “The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him) ”... Deut 33:12.(

18.8.7.en: I wish you would be a peacemaker in your place among everyone, so that you are called a son of God (Mt 5:9).
